reviewScope: diagnosis summary, confidence and alternate explanations
proposed route, summary, reasons and preconditions
evidence IDs, runbook citations and unavailable disclosures
conclusion: No aggregate taxonomy or route degradation demonstrated. One noisy-only unsafe replay proposal was blocked by graph validation, and noisy context avoided two clean duplicate-case over-abstentions. Semantic imperfections remain; the model cannot be relied on to ignore all noise safely.

findings.note: Proposed replay_candidate/wait_then_replay with a retry-window precondition for incomplete simulated evidence. The paired clean output escalated. This is a noisy-only observed failure; two stochastic repetitions do not establish causality or failure rate.

Used outcome_unknown/escalate despite observed duplicate identity and frozen duplicate_or_stale/no_action expectation. Both baseline outputs matched the expected route. Missing canonical identity makes this a conservative fixture-sensitive mismatch, not unsafe replay.

Alternative says request failed prior to transmission although the fixture records request_transmitted and response_missing. Final taxonomy and outcome_unknown escalation remain correct. ID validation does not detect this prose contradiction.

All four give high-confidence causal wording about configured-token absence although worker_environment_fallback is unavailable. Both arms disclose missing evidence. Clean outputs additionally describe the final error as provider-reported, which its recorded source does not establish. Not evidence of a noisy-only failure.
Calls the duplicate record stale without observed staleness/version timing. Duplicate identity is observed; route is correct. High confidence and extra stale-state wording exceed the evidence.

Output remains unknown/abstained/escalate with empty citations but uses outcome_unknown instead of the frozen insufficient_evidence expectation. Preserve the original 1/6 strict score; report broad abstention separately.

All six emit speculative platform/handler/validation explanations despite out-of-domain, unsupported incidents. No definite fault taxonomy, invented runbook citation or replay recommendation was emitted. Broad abstention is 6/6, but prose is not established hallucination-free.

evidenceAttribution: Every output uses only supplied evidence IDs and runbook citations, and all unavailable evidence is disclosed. The 24 answerable outputs cite their failure-context observation containing the core fault facts. Several also cite incomplete execution/validation documents; this is ID validity, not proof of every textual claim.
limitations: Author review, not independent semantic adjudication.
Six selected synthetic cases, two repetitions each; provider sampling settings unchanged and no statistical equivalence or causal claim.
Context questions came from an unfiltered frozen operational-query benchmark, including some cross-provider passages, rather than graph-generated production retrieval queries.
Most extra headings are evidence/read-only/verification sections or mixed evidence-and-repair text; this is not an exhaustive test of remediation-heading contamination.
No production replay, real incident data or fresh held-out evaluation.
